questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I am studying biology, it was important for me to be close to nature and Vancouver Island seemed like the perfect place.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UVic sends out tons of information, which can feel overwhelming, but in the end it was pretty easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Whenever I needed assistance, I just contacted the exchange team, and they responded super quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Victoria is experiencing a housing crisis, so it’s extremely difficult but manageable. I recommend using Facebook, Airbnb, and Vrbo. I found accommodation through Vrbo, which is very similar to Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most students live around campus in Gordon Head, but I lived in Fernwood and really enjoyed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
From what I understood, exchange students have priority, so you are nearly guaranteed to get the courses you want. 
You are given a date, after which you sign up on their website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email the exchange team if you have any questions. There is a limited amount of information about the courses, so it can be a good idea to sign up for more than you need, as you can drop courses during the first two weeks

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got everything i signed up for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be more bold when picking courses. Don’t limit yourself to what you are studying at home. 
I loved GEOG 303 – Conservation and Ecology of Whales and ES 361 – Biodiversity of British Columbia.
I also took BIOL 418 – Forest Ecology, which I loved and hated at the same time, as it was a lot of work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took Immunology and Forest Ecology. Both courses had a high workload, especially Forest Ecology, where there were continuous assignments and ongoing tasks throughout the term. The academic level itself was not overly difficult, but the courses required consistent effort and regular work to keep up.
Conservation and Ecology of Whales and Biodiversity of British Columbia were both very fun courses and had exactly the kind of workload you want on exchange, as they allowed time to explore while still being interesting classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is different because of midterms and many assignments. So even if the overall level is lower, it can still feel like a lot, as you constantly have to hand something in.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOL 418 – Forest Ecology
MICR 303 - Immunology
GEOG 303 – Conservation and Ecology of Whales
ES 361 – Biodiversity of British Columbia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Geog 303, ES 361

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is really expensive, and Walmart is the only affordable grocery store.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is relatively cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many clubs, and they all seemed super fun, but I didn’t sign up for any, as they require a lot of commitment and I preferred to spend my free time exploring the island on my days off.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, surfing and road trips. I spent a lot of time surfing at Jordan River, which is about an hour outside of town.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get lost, the island is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very friendly and welcoming but in school it can be hard to make new local friends

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I joined the Fernwood run club, which is not part of the university, but people were very welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It’s not really a cultural difference, but you need a car if you want to get around the island. So try to find some friends who want to rent a car with you, or consider buying one.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly when you’re exploring the island.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Joining a club makes it super easy to make friends.
Don’t pick very demanding classes. You want to spend your time exploring the island.
Choose classes that help you learn about the culture and nature of the island.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the fact that you can switch classes during the first two weeks. It makes choosing classes with limited information less stressful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to combine studying with experiencing a new country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studying and exploring, especially as I picked two very demanding classes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
